# Data Integration

## Purpose

The purpose of the data integration stage is to combine the different
datasets collected for the project into a structured analytical dataset
while preserving their original values, units, scope and provenance.

The source datasets cover different reporting periods, levels of
granularity and data structures. Integration is therefore required to
align common identifiers such as analytical year, facility, computing
system, resource type and Field of Research before the data can be
analysed together.

At this stage, integration focuses on organising and linking the available
information rather than forcing observations into common units or
classifications. Differences in naming, classification and compute units
are addressed subsequently through data standardisation and conversion.

Where datasets cannot be combined directly because of differences in
scope or granularity, those distinctions are retained explicitly rather
than assuming equivalence.

## Main Datasets

The integration process combines several datasets covering 2014 - 2026,
with different analytical roles.

The core HPC datasets include:

- yearly HPC demand and allocation source workbooks,
- Field of Research composition data, and
- HPC system and capacity information.

Supporting datasets include:

- research funding data, and
- research workforce and research activity data.

The core datasets provide the historical evidence used to construct
measures of requested compute, allocated compute and disciplinary
composition. Supporting datasets are retained as contextual or candidate
explanatory variables for later analysis and modelling.

Because these datasets differ in temporal coverage, granularity and
reporting scope, they are not merged indiscriminately. Integration is
performed only where suitable common identifiers and compatible levels
of aggregation are available.

Where annual demand or allocation measures are not directly available,
derived or proxy values are constructed later from the integrated source
evidence using explicitly documented assumptions. These selected annual
measures are subsequently assembled into a separate summary dataset for
modelling.

## Yearly Source Integration

The detailed yearly source files are integrated before constructing the
annual modelling summary.

For the HPC demand and allocation data, each yearly workbook contains
multiple types of evidence. The integration therefore preserves the
different analytical levels rather than reducing each workbook
immediately to a single annual value.

Three recurring components are retained:

- `Project_Allocations`, containing project- or allocation-level records,
- `Context_Metrics`, containing reported or derived annual and contextual
  measures, and
- `Resource_Envelope`, containing information on available resources and
  system-level capacity.

Field of Research data are integrated separately from the yearly
`FoR_Composition` sheets.

The source filename and source period are retained during integration so
that each observation remains traceable to its original yearly workbook.
The resulting integrated tables form the evidence base from which annual
summary measures are selected or derived later.

### Load Data & Libraries

Define Path

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)

demand_path <- "assets/data/raw data/demand and allocation"
for_path <- "assets/data/raw data/field of research"

clean_path <- "assets/data/data clean"
```

Get yearly demand/allocation files

```{r}
demand_files <- list.files(
  demand_path,
  pattern = "\\.xlsx$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

```

Derived the source period from file name.

```{r}
get_source_period <- function(path) {

  filename <- basename(path)

  years <- str_match(
    filename,
    "(\\d{4})_(\\d{2})"
  )

  paste0(
    years[, 2],
    "/",
    years[, 3]
  )
}

get_end_year <- function(source_period) {

  end_year <- str_extract(
    source_period,
    "(?<=/)\\d{2}$"
  )

  2000 + as.numeric(end_year)
}
```

Each yearly demand and allocation workbook contains several recurring
worksheets. The same set of yearly workbooks is therefore used to extract
each analytical component separately.

#### Integrate Context Metrics

Demand and allocation context metrics are combined across the yearly
workbooks.

These records contain annual or supporting measures used to interpret
requested compute, allocated compute and related demand-allocation
relationships.

```{r}
context_metrics <- map_dfr(
  demand_files,
  function(file) {

    read_excel(
      file,
      sheet = "Context_Metrics"
    ) |>
      mutate(
        source_file = basename(file),
        source_period = get_source_period(file)
      )
  }
)

```

#### Integrate Project Allocations

Project-level allocation records are combined across the yearly
workbooks while preserving their original source-level structure.

```{r}
project_allocations <- map_dfr(
  demand_files,
  function(file) {

    read_excel(
      file,
      sheet = "Project_Allocations",
      col_types = "text"
    ) |>
      mutate(
        source_file = basename(file),
        source_period = get_source_period(file)
      )
  }
)
```

#### Integrate Resource Envelope

Resource-envelope records are combined across the yearly workbooks.

These records describe available HPC systems, resource availability and
capacity-related information used to interpret the supply environment
associated with observed demand and allocation.

```{r}
resource_envelope <- map_dfr(
  demand_files,
  function(file) {

    read_excel(
      file,
      sheet = "Resource_Envelope",
      col_types = "text"
    ) |>
      mutate(
        source_file = basename(file),
        source_period = get_source_period(file)
      )
  }
)
```

#### Align Analytical Year

A common analytical year is created to align observations across the
different yearly source tables. The ending year of each source period is
used as the common reference year where a consistent NCMAS or allocation
year is not available.

```{r}
context_metrics <- context_metrics |>
  mutate(
    year = get_end_year(source_period)
  )

project_allocations <- project_allocations |>
  mutate(
    year = coalesce(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ncmas_year)),
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(allocation_year)),
      get_end_year(source_period)
    )
  )

resource_envelope <- resource_envelope |>
  mutate(
    year = coalesce(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ncmas_year)),
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(allocation_year)),
      get_end_year(source_period)
    )
  )
```

#### Validate Demand and Allocation Integration

The integrated demand and allocation tables are checked to confirm that
all yearly source workbooks have been retained and that the common
analytical year is aligned consistently across the historical series.

```{r}
context_metrics |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    source_periods = n_distinct(source_period),
    source_files = n_distinct(source_file),
    years = n_distinct(year)
  )

project_allocations |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    source_periods = n_distinct(source_period),
    source_files = n_distinct(source_file),
    years = n_distinct(year)
  )

resource_envelope |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    source_periods = n_distinct(source_period),
    source_files = n_distinct(source_file),
    years = n_distinct(year)
  )
```

#### Integrate Field of Research Data

Field of Research composition data are combined across the yearly FoR
workbooks while retaining the source filename and reporting period.

These records describe the disciplinary composition of HPC allocation
and are integrated separately from the demand and allocation evidence
because they have a different analytical structure and level of
aggregation.

```{r}
for_files <- list.files(
  for_path,
  pattern = "\\.xlsx$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
for_data <- map_dfr(
  for_files,
  function(file) {

    read_excel(
      file,
      sheet = "FoR_Composition",
      col_types = "text"
    ) |>
      mutate(
        source_file = basename(file)
      )
  }
)
```

```{r}
for_data <- for_data |>
  mutate(
    year = get_end_year(source_period)
  )
```

#### Validate Field of Research Integration

The integrated Field of Research data are checked to confirm that all
yearly FoR workbooks have been retained and that the common analytical
year is aligned consistently with the demand and allocation series.

```{r}
for_data |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    source_periods = n_distinct(source_period),
    source_files = n_distinct(source_file),
    years = n_distinct(year)
  )
```

```{r}
for_data |>
  group_by(source_period, year) |>
  summarise(
    composition_total = sum(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(composition_pct)),
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

#### Export Integrated Source Data

The validated integrated tables are exported as a consolidated workbook
to provide a reproducible intermediate dataset between the original yearly
source files and the annual modelling summary.

The workbook retains the different analytical components on separate
worksheets so that differences in granularity and scope are preserved.

```{r}
writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    Context_Metrics = context_metrics,
    Project_Allocations = project_allocations,
    Resource_Envelope = resource_envelope,
    FoR_Composition = for_data
  ),
  path = file.path(
    clean_path,
    "integrated_hpc_source_data.xlsx"
  )
)
```


## Annual Demand and Allocation Summary Construction

The annual demand and allocation summary is constructed after integration
of the detailed yearly source evidence.

The existing manually assembled summary is retained temporarily as a
reference for reconciliation rather than treated as an independent source
of data. Each annual requested and allocated compute value is checked
against the integrated `Context_Metrics`, `Project_Allocations` and
`Resource_Envelope` evidence.

Where a directly reported comparable annual value is available, that
value is preferred. Where it is not available, a derived or proxy value
may be constructed from the integrated evidence using an explicitly
documented assumption.

```{r}
current_summary <- read_excel(
  file.path(clean_path, "demand_allocation_data.xlsx")
) |>
  mutate(
    year = get_end_year(source_period)
  )
```

### Reconstruct Annual Demand and Allocation Summary

Annual demand and allocation measures are reconstructed from the
integrated source tables before comparison with the previously assembled
summary.

Context metrics are used to identify reported annual totals, ratios and
derived demand information. Project-level allocations and resource
envelopes are retained as supporting evidence and are aggregated only
where their scope and units are sufficiently consistent.

```{r}
context_candidates <- context_metrics |>
  mutate(
    value_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))
  ) |>
  filter(
    str_detect(
      metric,
      regex(
        "request|demand|allocat|fulfil|oversub|capacity|available",
        ignore_case = TRUE
      )
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,
    metric,
    value_num,
    unit,
    scope,
    source,
    notes
  ) |>
  arrange(year, metric)
```

```{r}
project_candidates <- project_allocations |>
  mutate(
    allocated_compute_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(allocated_compute))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(allocated_compute_num)) |>
  group_by(
    year,
    source_period,
    unit,
    allocation_type
  ) |>
  summarise(
    allocated_total = sum(allocated_compute_num),
    records = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, unit, allocation_type)
```

```{r}
resource_candidates <- resource_envelope |>
  mutate(
    resource_available_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(resource_available))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(resource_available_num)) |>
  group_by(
    year,
    source_period,
    unit
  ) |>
  summarise(
    resource_available_total =
      sum(resource_available_num),
    records = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, unit)
```

```{r}
context_candidates |>
  count(year)

project_candidates |>
  count(year)

resource_candidates |>
  count(year)
```

### Construct Reconstructed Annual Summary

The annual series is reconstructed from the integrated evidence without
using the previously assembled summary as an input.

Directly reported annual values are used where available. Derived values
are calculated only where the required source values and relationships are
contained in the integrated evidence. Where the integrated evidence is
insufficient to reproduce an earlier summary value, the value is left
missing for subsequent reconciliation rather than being inferred from the
existing summary.

```{r}
get_metric_value <- function(target_year, metric_name) {

  context_candidates |>
    filter(
      year == target_year,
      metric == metric_name
    ) |>
    pull(value_num) |>
    first()
}
```

```{r}
reconstructed_summary <- tibble(
  year = 2014:2026,
  source_period = paste0(
    year - 1,
    "/",
    str_sub(as.character(year), -2)
  )
) |>
  mutate(

    requested_compute = case_when(

      year == 2014 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2014,
          "ncmas_total_ksu_request"
        ),

      year == 2015 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2015,
          "nci_ncmas_implied_demand_2015"
        ),

      year == 2016 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2016,
          "nci_ncmas_implied_requested_compute_2016"
        ),

      year == 2017 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2017,
          "pawsey_ncmas_requested_compute_2017"
        ),

      year == 2018 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2018,
          "national_implied_requested_compute_2018"
        ),

      # Current integrated evidence does not contain the
      # 220 × 3 national proxy used previously.
      year == 2019 ~ NA_real_,

      year == 2020 ~
        resource_candidates |>
          filter(
            year == 2020,
            unit == "kSU"
          ) |>
          pull(resource_available_total) |>
          first() * 2,

      year == 2021 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2021,
          "direct_ncmas_2021_total_allocation"
        ) *
        get_metric_value(
          2021,
          "ncmas_demand_supply_factor_high"
        ),

      year == 2022 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2022,
          "ncmas_allocated_compute_total"
        ) /
        (
          get_metric_value(
            2022,
            "ncmas_allocated_share_of_requested_pct"
          ) / 100
        ),

      year == 2023 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2023,
          "ncmas_requested_compute"
        ),

      # Retrospective 57% and 56% demand relationships are
      # not currently retained in the integrated source tables.
      year == 2024 ~ NA_real_,
      year == 2025 ~ NA_real_,

      year == 2026 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2026,
          "ncmas_requested_compute"
        )
    ),

    allocated_compute = case_when(

      # 83,505 kSU is not currently retained as an annual
      # metric in the integrated evidence.
      year == 2014 ~ NA_real_,

      year == 2015 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2015,
          "nci_ncmas_allocation_2014_15"
        ),

      year == 2016 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2016,
          "nci_ncmas_allocation_2015_16"
        ),

      year == 2017 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2017,
          "pawsey_ncmas_available_compute_2017"
        ),

      year == 2018 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2018,
          "national_allocated_compute_2018"
        ),

      # The 220m national capacity proxy is not currently
      # retained in the integrated evidence.
      year == 2019 ~ NA_real_,

      year == 2020 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2020,
          "nci_supplement_ncmas_allocation_total_verified"
        ),

      year == 2021 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2021,
          "direct_ncmas_2021_total_allocation"
        ),

      year == 2022 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2022,
          "ncmas_allocated_compute_total"
        ),

      year == 2023 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2023,
          "ncmas_allocated_compute_total"
        ),

      year == 2024 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2024,
          "ncmas_total_allocation"
        ),

      year == 2025 ~
        get_metric_value(
          2025,
          "ncmas_total_allocation"
        ),

      year == 2026 ~
        get_metric_value(2026, "ncmas_gadi_allocation") +
        get_metric_value(2026, "ncmas_setonix_cpu_allocation") +
        get_metric_value(2026, "ncmas_setonix_gpu_allocation")
    )
  )
```

```{r}
reconstructed_summary
```

### Compare Reconstructed and Existing Annual Summaries

The reconstructed annual series is compared with the previously assembled
summary to identify values that are reproduced directly from the
integrated evidence and values that require additional source evidence or
documented derivation.

```{r}
current_summary <- read_excel(
  file.path(clean_path, "demand_allocation_data.xlsx")
) |>
  mutate(
    year = get_end_year(source_period)
  )
```

```{r}
summary_comparison <- current_summary |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,
    old_requested = requested_compute,
    old_allocated = allocated_compute
  ) |>
  full_join(
    reconstructed_summary |>
      rename(
        reconstructed_requested = requested_compute,
        reconstructed_allocated = allocated_compute
      ),
    by = c("year", "source_period")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    requested_match = case_when(
      is.na(reconstructed_requested) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ near(old_requested, reconstructed_requested)
    ),
    allocated_match = case_when(
      is.na(reconstructed_allocated) ~ FALSE,
      TRUE ~ near(old_allocated, reconstructed_allocated)
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(year)
```

```{r}
summary_comparison |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,
    old_requested,
    reconstructed_requested,
    requested_match,
    old_allocated,
    reconstructed_allocated,
    allocated_match
  )
```

### Resolve Unreconstructed Annual Values

The initial reconstruction identified several annual values that could not
be reproduced from the integrated source tables because the supporting
metric or derivation had not yet been retained explicitly in the
integrated evidence.

These cases are reviewed against the original yearly source evidence
before the final annual summary is constructed.

```{r}
unreconstructed_values <- summary_comparison |>
  filter(
    is.na(reconstructed_requested) |
    is.na(reconstructed_allocated)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    year,
    source_period,
    missing_requested = is.na(reconstructed_requested),
    missing_allocated = is.na(reconstructed_allocated),
    old_requested,
    old_allocated
  )

unreconstructed_values
```

```{r}
missing_value_notes <- tribble(
  ~year, ~missing_measure, ~reason,

  2014, "Allocated compute",
  "The 83,505 kSU annual allocation is supported by the original annual-report evidence but was not retained as an explicit annual metric in the integrated Context_Metrics table.",

  2019, "Requested and allocated compute",
  "The 660 million requested / 220 million available proxy pair depends on the reported three-times demand-to-supply relationship, but the complete derivation is not retained explicitly in the integrated evidence.",

  2024, "Requested compute",
  "The requested-demand proxy depends on the retrospective 57% allocation-to-request relationship, which is not currently retained as an explicit integrated metric.",

  2025, "Requested compute",
  "The requested-demand proxy depends on the retrospective 56% allocation-to-request relationship, which is not currently retained as an explicit integrated metric."
)
```

### Derive Missing Annual Measures

Where a directly reported annual demand or allocation measure is not
available, a derived or proxy value is constructed from other published
evidence retained in the integrated source data.

These derivations are applied only where the relationship used is
explicitly supported by the source material. Derived and proxy values are
retained separately from directly reported measures so that their status
remains transparent.

```{r}
reconstructed_summary <- reconstructed_summary |>
  mutate(
    requested_compute = case_when(
      year == 2019 ~ 220 * 3,
      year == 2024 ~ 812569 / 0.57,
      year == 2025 ~ 876200 / 0.56,
      TRUE ~ requested_compute
    ),
    allocated_compute = case_when(
      year == 2014 ~ 83505,
      year == 2019 ~ 220,
      TRUE ~ allocated_compute
    )
  )
```

```{r}
reconstructed_summary <- reconstructed_summary |>
  mutate(
    requested_basis = case_when(
      year == 2014 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2015 ~ "Derived",
      year == 2016 ~ "Derived",
      year == 2017 ~ "Proxy",
      year == 2018 ~ "Derived",
      year == 2019 ~ "Derived proxy",
      year == 2020 ~ "Derived proxy",
      year == 2021 ~ "Derived proxy",
      year == 2022 ~ "Derived proxy",
      year == 2023 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2024 ~ "Derived proxy",
      year == 2025 ~ "Derived proxy",
      year == 2026 ~ "Direct"
    ),

    allocated_basis = case_when(
      year == 2014 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2015 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2016 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2017 ~ "Capacity proxy",
      year == 2018 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2019 ~ "Capacity proxy",
      year == 2020 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2021 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2022 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2023 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2024 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2025 ~ "Direct",
      year == 2026 ~ "Direct comparable subset"
    ),

    derivation_note = case_when(
      year == 2015 ~
        "Requested compute derived from reported allocation and demand relationship.",

      year == 2016 ~
        "Requested compute derived from reported one-third fulfilment relationship.",

      year == 2017 ~
        "Requested compute retained as a lower-bound proxy; available capacity used as the allocation proxy.",

      year == 2018 ~
        "Requested compute derived from 222 million hours and a 42% fulfilment relationship.",

      year == 2019 ~
        "Requested compute derived as 220 × 3; available capacity used as the allocation proxy.",

      year == 2020 ~
        "Requested compute derived from the resource envelope and reported demand-supply relationship.",

      year == 2021 ~
        "Requested compute derived using the approximate three-times demand-supply relationship.",

      year == 2022 ~
        "Requested compute derived from allocated compute and the reported 50% fulfilment relationship.",

      year == 2024 ~
        "Requested compute derived from allocated compute and the retrospective 57% fulfilment relationship.",

      year == 2025 ~
        "Requested compute derived from allocated compute and the retrospective 56% fulfilment relationship.",

      year == 2026 ~
        "Setonix-Q excluded from allocation to match the scope of the published requested-compute comparison.",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

```{r}
reconstructed_summary
```

### Final Reconciliation Check

After the missing annual measures are reconstructed and their basis is
documented, the annual series is compared again with the previously
assembled summary.

This final check identifies whether the reconstructed values reproduce the
existing annual summary and highlights any remaining differences due to
rounding, scope or methodological treatment.

```{r}
final_summary_comparison <- current_summary |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,
    old_requested = requested_compute,
    old_allocated = allocated_compute
  ) |>
  full_join(
    reconstructed_summary |>
      select(
        year,
        source_period,
        reconstructed_requested = requested_compute,
        reconstructed_allocated = allocated_compute,
        requested_basis,
        allocated_basis,
        derivation_note
      ),
    by = c("year", "source_period")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    requested_difference =
      reconstructed_requested - old_requested,

    allocated_difference =
      reconstructed_allocated - old_allocated,

    requested_match =
      near(
        old_requested,
        reconstructed_requested,
        tol = 1e-3
      ),

    allocated_match =
      near(
        old_allocated,
        reconstructed_allocated,
        tol = 1e-3
      )
  ) |>
  arrange(year)
```

```{r}
final_summary_comparison |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,
    old_requested,
    reconstructed_requested,
    requested_match,
    old_allocated,
    reconstructed_allocated,
    allocated_match
  )
```

```{r}
final_summary_comparison |>
  summarise(
    years = n(),
    requested_matches = sum(requested_match),
    allocated_matches = sum(allocated_match),
    requested_mismatches = sum(!requested_match),
    allocated_mismatches = sum(!allocated_match)
  )
```

### Export Reconciled Annual Demand and Allocation Summary

Following reconciliation, the reconstructed annual series is retained as
the reproducible demand and allocation summary for subsequent
standardisation, conversion and modelling.

The exported dataset preserves the analytical basis of each annual value
so that directly reported, derived and proxy measures remain
distinguishable in later stages of the analysis.

```{r}
final_demand_allocation_summary <- reconstructed_summary |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,
    requested_compute,
    allocated_compute,
    requested_basis,
    allocated_basis,
    derivation_note
  )

final_demand_allocation_summary
```

```{r}
writexl::write_xlsx(
  final_demand_allocation_summary,
  path = file.path(
    clean_path,
    "reconciled_demand_allocation_summary.xlsx"
  )
)
```

## Field of Research Summary Construction

The integrated Field of Research records are next assembled into a
consistent annual summary.

Unlike the national demand and allocation series, historical FoR evidence
varies in classification, reporting scope and completeness. The purpose
of this stage is therefore to preserve the reported disciplinary
composition while identifying differences in coverage and evidence
quality across years.

FoR percentages are treated primarily as allocation composition rather
than directly observed demand composition. Where these shares are later
applied to annual requested compute, the resulting values are treated as
analytical demand proxies rather than observed FoR-specific demand.

```{r}
for_annual_check <- for_data |>
  mutate(
    composition_pct_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(composition_pct))
  ) |>
  group_by(
    year,
    source_period
  ) |>
  summarise(
    records = n(),
    composition_total =
      sum(composition_pct_num, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year)

for_annual_check
```

```{r}
for_data |>
  count(
    year,
    source_period,
    evidence_quality,
    scope,
    value_basis
  ) |>
  arrange(year)
```

```{r}
for_quality_summary <- for_data |>
  mutate(
    composition_pct_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(composition_pct))
  ) |>
  group_by(
    year,
    source_period,
    evidence_quality,
    scope,
    value_basis
  ) |>
  summarise(
    records = n(),
    composition_total =
      sum(composition_pct_num, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year)

for_quality_summary
```

### Assess Historical FoR Comparability

The yearly FoR compositions generally sum to approximately 100%, but
completeness alone does not imply that all years are directly comparable.

Historical observations differ in reporting scope, classification method
and evidence quality. Some years are based on direct NCMAS allocation
composition, while others rely on estimated project classification,
residual categories, or broader facility-level usage.

For this reason, the FoR series is classified by analytical use rather
than treated as a uniformly consistent time series. The strongest and most
comparable national NCMAS composition evidence is available from 2021
onward. Earlier observations are retained primarily as historical context,
with 2017 treated separately because it represents Pawsey usage across all
allocation schemes rather than national NCMAS allocation composition.

```{r}
for_year_quality <- for_annual_check |>
  mutate(
    analytical_use = case_when(
      year == 2017 ~ "Context only",
      year <= 2020 ~ "Historical / lower confidence",
      year >= 2021 ~ "Main FoR trend"
    )
  )

for_year_quality
```

```{r}
for_year_quality <- for_annual_check |>
  mutate(
    analytical_use = case_when(
      year == 2017 ~ "Context only",
      year %in% c(2014, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2020) ~
        "Historical / lower confidence",
      year == 2015 ~
        "Historical / moderate confidence",
      year >= 2021 ~
        "Main FoR trend"
    )
  )
```

### Construct FoR-Level Compute Measures

The annual FoR composition is linked to the reconciled national demand and
allocation series using analytical year and source period.

FoR allocation shares are used to estimate the amount of annual allocated
compute associated with each research field. The same shares are also
applied to annual requested compute to construct an indicative FoR-level
demand proxy.

The resulting demand measure is not treated as directly observed
disciplinary demand because the available FoR percentages primarily
describe allocation composition rather than request composition.

```{r}
for_summary <- for_data |>
  mutate(
    composition_pct_num =
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(composition_pct))
  ) |>
  left_join(
    for_year_quality |>
      select(
        year,
        source_period,
        analytical_use
      ),
    by = c("year", "source_period")
  )
```

```{r}
for_summary <- for_summary |>
  left_join(
    final_demand_allocation_summary |>
      select(
        year,
        source_period,
        requested_compute,
        allocated_compute,
        requested_basis,
        allocated_basis
      ),
    by = c("year", "source_period")
  )
```

```{r}
for_summary <- for_summary |>
  mutate(
    allocation_share_for =
      composition_pct_num / 100,

    allocated_compute_for =
      allocated_compute * allocation_share_for,

    estimated_demand_by_for_proxy =
      requested_compute * allocation_share_for
  )
```

```{r}
for_summary |>
  group_by(
    year,
    source_period
  ) |>
  summarise(
    composition_total =
      sum(composition_pct_num, na.rm = TRUE),

    allocated_for_total =
      sum(allocated_compute_for, na.rm = TRUE),

    demand_proxy_total =
      sum(estimated_demand_by_for_proxy, na.rm = TRUE),

    annual_allocated =
      first(allocated_compute),

    annual_requested =
      first(requested_compute),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(year)
```

The validation confirms that the FoR composition shares sum to 100% for
each analytical year. As a result, the sum of FoR-level allocated compute
reproduces the corresponding annual allocated-compute total, while the sum
of the FoR-level demand proxies reproduces the annual requested-compute
total.

This confirms that the FoR allocation shares have been applied
consistently to the reconciled national series. The demand values remain
analytical proxies rather than directly observed FoR-specific requests.

### Export Reconciled Field of Research Summary

The validated FoR-level measures are retained as the integrated
disciplinary summary for subsequent standardisation, analysis and
modelling.

The exported table preserves the original FoR classification information,
allocation composition, analytical-use classification and evidence-quality
metadata. FoR-level requested compute remains explicitly identified as a
proxy derived from allocation composition.

```{r}
final_for_summary <- for_summary |>
  select(
    year,
    source_period,

    research_field_reported,
    for_2008_division_code,
    for_2020_division_code,
    for_standard_2020,

    composition_pct = composition_pct_num,
    allocation_share_for,

    requested_compute_annual = requested_compute,
    allocated_compute_annual = allocated_compute,

    estimated_demand_by_for_proxy,
    allocated_compute_for,

    requested_basis,
    allocated_basis,

    analytical_use,
    evidence_quality,
    scope,
    value_basis,
    classification_status,
    standardisation_note,
    notes,
    source,
    source_url
  ) |>
  arrange(
    year,
    desc(composition_pct)
  )
```

```{r}
final_for_summary |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    years = n_distinct(year),
    source_periods = n_distinct(source_period),
    missing_composition = sum(is.na(composition_pct)),
    missing_for_name = sum(is.na(for_standard_2020))
  )
```

```{r}
writexl::write_xlsx(
  final_for_summary,
  path = file.path(
    clean_path,
    "reconciled_field_of_research_summary.xlsx"
  )
)
```
